chapter: Algiers parades and the wider city
title: Mardi Gras and parades on the Algiers side
summary: People from New Orleans came to Algiers at Mardi Gras; a white club had a parade and hired his three-piece field band.

venues.name: Odd Fellows Hall on Siglin Street

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: I think that's just died about a year or more. Yeah, that's right. Well, at least there's people there. Eddie, wasn't it?

Richard. Yeah, yeah. A couple of them were over in the blocks. Yeah. And they really had a nice band, too. I was guilty. What about on Mardi Gras Day? Did they have much going on over here, lower than when they do now?
Oh, gee, we used to take people coming from New Orleans over here.

Over here, is it clear? They had that hall I told you down there, down on Siglin Street, the Outfellas Hall, and you couldn't pass there for the people there during that time. And they had right down here on Tash and Newton, they had a place right there, and you couldn't pass around there for the people. People used to come over here from New Orleans. They didn't have parades just like they have in New Orleans. Down at the white club down there, called Prama Place, they had a big club there. They used to parade all around there, they didn't go in New Orleans. They had about a hundred and some odd members in there. We used to play for them. That's how we had the field band then, during that time, three pieces. We used to play for them. Just three pieces?
Piccolo, snare drum, and a bass drum.
